title: What actually happens to skin structure in your thirties
summary: Not everything that changes with age is visible yet. Here is what is happening underneath, and why it matters now.
body:
Most visible signs of ageing are described as skin changes, but many begin structurally, in volume, bone and muscle, well before the surface shows anything.

Understanding this distinction changes what's worth addressing early. A plan built around structure and surface together tends to hold up better over time than one focused on the skin alone.

This is also why a consultation in your thirties looks different from one later on: the priority is usually establishing a baseline and slowing structural change, rather than reversing it. Assessment at this stage is as much about direction as it is about the treatment itself.
